title: NALSA — Legal Services Frequently Asked Questions

service_context.subject: Free legal services, legal aid eligibility and access
service_context.purpose: Provide reliable information about legal services, free legal aid, eligibility and access to Legal Services Institutions.
service_context.important_note: This source provides information about accessing legal services. It must not be used by the AI to determine the outcome of a user's legal case.

legal_services.definition: Legal services include services connected with the conduct of a case or other legal proceeding before a court, authority or tribunal, as well as advice on legal matters.
free_legal_aid_may_include: Representation by an advocate in legal proceedings.
Payment of process fees, witness expenses and other appropriate charges connected with legal proceedings.
Preparation of pleadings, memoranda of appeal and paper books, including printing and translation of documents.
Drafting of legal documents and special leave petitions.
Supply of certified copies of judgments, orders, notes of evidence and other documents.
legal_services.additional_support: Free legal services may also include aid and advice for accessing benefits under welfare statutes and government schemes and for ensuring access to justice.

legal_aid_vs_legal_advice.legal_aid: Legal aid includes legal representation by a lawyer assigned through the concerned Legal Services Authority.
legal_aid_vs_legal_advice.legal_advice_and_assistance: Legal advice and assistance includes advice on general areas of law and assistance provided by lawyers associated with Legal Services Institutions.
legal_aid_vs_legal_advice.important_point: A person who does not fall within the eligibility criteria for free legal aid under Section 12 may still be able to obtain legal advice and assistance from Legal Services Institutions.

eligibility.statutory_basis: Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
categories: A member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
A victim of trafficking in human beings or begar.
A person with a disability or mental illness as covered by the applicable law.
A person facing circumstances of undeserved want such as mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster.
A person in custody, including specified protective, juvenile or mental-health institutions.
A person satisfying the applicable income criteria prescribed for the relevant court and jurisdiction.

women.rule: A woman is eligible to apply for free legal aid irrespective of her income or financial status under Section 12(c) of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

eligibility.genuine_case_requirement: NALSA's FAQ states that a person satisfying the Section 12 criteria is entitled to legal services provided the concerned Legal Services Institution is satisfied that the person has a genuine case to prosecute or defend.

access_and_scope.types_of_cases: Free legal aid is not restricted to a particular type of case. A person satisfying the applicable eligibility criteria may seek legal services for a case to be prosecuted or defended.
access_and_scope.consultation_only: A person may seek legal consultation or advice even when they do not intend to pursue a court case.
access_and_scope.stage_of_case: Eligible persons may apply for free legal aid at different stages of a case, including at the appeal stage.

fees.legal_services_cost: Legal services provided by Legal Services Institutions are free of cost to eligible beneficiaries.
fees.application_fee: There is no charge for obtaining or submitting an application form for free legal aid.

additional_points.previous_private_lawyer: A person may still apply for free legal aid after having been represented by a private lawyer, subject to the applicable procedure.
additional_points.second_opinion: NALSA's FAQ states that a person who has engaged a private lawyer may also obtain a second opinion from panel lawyers.
additional_points.confidentiality: NALSA states that personal information of clients approaching Legal Services Authorities is kept confidential.
additional_points.appeals: Free legal aid may be available for challenging orders of High Courts or the Supreme Court, subject to eligibility requirements.

rag_use: Answer questions about who can seek free legal aid.
Explain that women are eligible for free legal aid irrespective of income or financial status.
Explain what services may be included in free legal aid.
Distinguish legal representation from general legal advice and assistance.
Explain that legal aid can be available at different stages of a case.
Provide information about accessing Legal Services Institutions.
Use the FAQ as a service-navigation source rather than a source for deciding legal entitlement.

application_to_alimony_plus.routing_rule: When the Alimony Plus user may benefit from legal representation or legal advice, the AI can use this source to explain available legal-aid pathways and eligibility information.
application_to_alimony_plus.safety_rule: The AI must not guarantee that a person will receive legal aid or that a case will succeed. It should provide the official eligibility and access information and recommend confirmation with the relevant Legal Services Institution when necessary.
application_to_alimony_plus.human_review: Questions requiring interpretation of individual facts, legal representation, or case-specific legal advice should be directed to an appropriate legal professional or Legal Services Institution.
